title: Shadow eval metrics: implement cardinality guardrails (tag allowlists + bucketing) with load-test + backpressure behavior
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Context
Shadow Traffic emits a new family of signals under shadow_eval.* that are used by Console dashboards + rollout policy gates. Current v0 instrumentation includes a handful of dimensions that can explode cardinality (e.g., per-route freeform names, per-shadow-target identifiers, ad hoc tags from judge modules). During beta load tests we saw ingestion pressure + noisy dashboards caused by uncontrolled label values. This issue implements hard cardinality guardrails with clear drop behavior + backpressure so that shadow traffic cannot take down the telemetry pipeline.

References
- Confluence: Observability standards – Shadow eval metrics schema + tagging: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/shadow-eval-metrics-schema-and-tagging.json
- Drive: Shadow metrics cardinality review: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/observability/shadow-metrics-cardinality-review.json
- SRE load testing plan: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/shadow-runner-load-test-plan-sheet.json
- Related work: ENG-2427 (telemetry pipeline join + aggregated tables), ENG-2419 (shadow runner execution), ENG-2440 (SRE alerts/budgets)

Problem statement
We need to:
1) Prevent high-cardinality tags from reaching metrics sinks (stats/histograms/counters).
2) Provide stable, documented tag semantics so dashboards and policy-gates don’t break.
3) Ensure failure modes are safe: dropping labels should never block primary traffic; shadow-only work can degrade gracefully.
4) Make it observable when we’re dropping/aggregating so customers/internal users trust the results.

Scope
- Implement tag allowlists at emission time (service SDK / instrumentation wrapper) for shadow_eval.* metrics.
- Implement bucketing/normalization rules for allowed tags where values are unbounded.
- Implement sink-side guardrails (ingestion/telemetry pipeline) as a second line of defense: reject/drop disallowed tags and increment a dropped counter.
- Add load tests to validate cardinality is bounded under worst-case sampling + per-route churn.
- Define backpressure behavior when cardinality guardrails trigger frequently (e.g., >N drops/min).

Non-goals
- Rewriting the whole telemetry pipeline.
- Changing the semantics of per-request shadow event logs (those are handled in ENG-2427); this ticket focuses on metrics dimensions and guardrails.

Design decisions (final)
1) Allowlist-based tagging for shadow_eval.*
- Explicit allowlist of tag keys per metric family (shadow_eval.*). Any other tag key is dropped.
- Explicit allowlist/normalization of tag values for certain keys (e.g., region must match known regions; unknown becomes "other").
- Important: request_id MUST NOT be a metric tag (always disallowed). If we need joinability, it lives in tracing/log events only.

2) Stable required dimensions (bounded)
All shadow_eval metrics must include:
- env: {prod, staging}
- region: {us-east, us-west, eu-central, ap-south, other}
- route_id: stable internal ID (NOT freeform route name)
- primary_model: normalized model identifier (from catalog), e.g., "llama-3.1-70b"; unknown => "other"
- shadow_target: normalized shadow target key (see below)

Optional, bounded dimensions (allowed only where documented)
- customer_tier: {free, pro, enterprise, internal, unknown}
- deployment_mode: {hosted, dedicated, private}
- shadow_outcome: {success, error, timeout, dropped}
- error_class: {timeout, capacity, upstream_5xx, invalid_config, judge_error, unknown}

3) Shadow target normalization
Problem: shadow targets can be configured per-route and could create unbounded unique identifiers.
Decision:
- Emit shadow_target as a small, stable identifier derived from config but bounded:
  - If the config includes a human-provided shadow target name, we do NOT pass it through.
  - We bucket by (shadow_model, quant_profile, prompt_config_version) into a normalized string with strict validation.
  - Additionally, we cap the number of distinct shadow_target values per route_id per 24h window in the pipeline; overflow buckets into "shadow_target=other".

4) Numeric bucketing
Some tags were being emitted as stringified numerics. Those are converted to histograms OR bucketed enums:
- prompt_tokens_bucket: {0-128, 129-256, 257-512, 513-1k, 1k-2k, 2k+}
- completion_tokens_bucket: same buckets
- latency_ms is emitted as histogram only (no per-request tag)
- judge_score is emitted as histogram + a coarse bucket tag {0-0.2, 0.2-0.4, 0.4-0.6, 0.6-0.8, 0.8-1.0}

5) Backpressure behavior
When the guardrail drops tags (or when the sink-side cap forces "other"), we emit:
- shadow_eval.dropped_total{reason=<reason>, region, env}++
Reasons:
- disallowed_tag_key
- disallowed_tag_value
- shadow_target_overflow
- route_overflow

Additionally, when dropped_total rate exceeds threshold (default: 5% of shadow_eval.run_started over 5m, per region):
- The shadow runner will switch to "minimal metrics mode" for 15 minutes (feature flaggable): only emits run_started/run_completed counters + latency histogram with required dimensions only.
- This is shadow-only; it MUST NOT change primary response path. This mode is surfaced in dashboards via shadow_eval.minimal_metrics_mode{region} gauge = 1.

Implementation plan
A) Emission-time guardrails (preferred)
- Add a shadow_eval metrics wrapper used by shadow runner + judge modules:
  - enforceTagAllowlist(metric_name, tags)
  - normalizeTags(tags) (region normalization, model normalization, tier mapping)
  - bucketTags(tags) (token buckets, judge score buckets)
- Enforce that route_name, request_id, user_id, prompt_hash are not emitted as tags.
- Add unit tests that validate:
  - disallowed tags are dropped
  - required tags are always present (or defaulted)
  - bucketing matches spec

B) Sink-side guardrails
- Update telemetry ingestion to drop any tag keys outside the allowlist for metric namespace shadow_eval.*
- Add per-metric cap in the aggregator: max distinct series per (region, env) per 10m window; above cap, force overflow to "other" and increment dropped_total with reason shadow_target_overflow/route_overflow.

C) Dashboard / alert wiring support (SRE)
- Ensure shadow_eval.dropped_total is available to Grafana panels and can be alerted.
- Add a recommended alert:
  - Warning: dropped_total / run_started > 1% for 10m
  - Page: dropped_total / run_started > 5% for 10m (paired with queue depth paging in ENG-2440)

Acceptance criteria
- No shadow_eval.* metric contains request_id, prompt content, route_name, or any freeform customer-provided string as a tag.
- For a fixed set of routes and shadow targets, time-series count stays within expected range (documented below).
- Under adversarial input (1000 unique route names / 1000 unique shadow target names), telemetry series count remains bounded and dropped_total increases appropriately.
- Minimal metrics mode engages automatically when drop rate is above threshold and returns to normal after cooldown.
- Load test demonstrates no measurable impact to primary path latency (verified via perf canary) and no telemetry pipeline saturation (no ingestion errors attributable to shadow_eval series).

Cardinality budget (documented)
- Per (env, region): max 50 routes * 4 shadow_targets * 3 outcome * ~5 optional dims => O(3k–5k) time series per metric, worst-case.
- Hard cap enforced in sink: 10k series per metric per (env, region) per 10m; overflow collapses into "other".

Testing
- Unit tests: tag allowlist, normalization, bucketing.
- Integration tests: shadow runner emits metrics with a synthetic config containing disallowed tags; verify sink drops and increments dropped_total.
- Load test: run sampling 5%/10%/20% in staging across 3 regions with synthetic high-churn routes; confirm stable series count and no ingestion error spikes.

Rollout plan
- Stage 1: ship emission-time guardrails behind feature flag shadow_eval_tag_guardrails (default on in staging).
- Stage 2: enable in prod for internal routes only (env=prod, customer_tier=internal), monitor dropped_total and series count.
- Stage 3: enable for beta accounts, paired with dashboards panel showing drops and minimal-metrics mode.
- Keep sink-side guardrails always-on for shadow_eval.* once deployed (defense in depth).

Open questions (resolved)
- Q: Should we allow customer_id as a metric tag for slicing? A: No; use customer_tier + dedicated/private/hosted, and join customer_id only in curated analytics tables (ENG-2427).
- Q: Can we tag by prompt_config_version? A: Yes, but only as a small integer bucketed into {v0, v1, v2, v3plus} to prevent churn; full version is available in event logs/analytics.

Status updates
- 2025-10-28 (Thomas): Drafted allowlist + normalization spec; synced with Allison Grant (Observability standards) and Sean Gallagher (SRE). Added sink-side cap proposal.
- 2025-11-03 (Thomas): Implemented emission wrapper in shadow runner; removed request_id + route_name tags from metrics. Added dropped_total counter + reasons.
- 2025-11-07 (Sean): Requested minimal metrics mode when drops exceed threshold; added to scope. Also asked for a dashboard panel showing drop ratio per region.
- 2025-11-12 (Thomas): Added minimal metrics mode (15m cooldown) + gauge. Added integration test in telemetry staging.
- 2025-11-18 (Logan): Load test results look good; series count bounded; drop ratio <0.5% for normal configs; adversarial test triggers minimal mode without pipeline errors.

Deliverables / links
- PRs (redwood):
  - Add shadow_eval tag allowlist + bucketing wrapper (internal): PR TBD
  - Telemetry sink-side allowlist enforcement for shadow_eval.* (internal): PR TBD
- Dashboards/alerts: handled in ENG-2440 / observability-pack wiring, but this ticket provides the dropped_total/minimal_metrics_mode signals.

Notes for support/PM
- If customers ask why certain breakdowns aren’t available (e.g., per-customer/per-request), answer: intentional to protect system reliability; we provide curated analytics tables and allowlisted breakdowns only.
- If customers see shadow_target=other, it indicates they exceeded the per-route shadow target series budget or used high-churn configs; recommend naming/organizing targets to reuse normalized (model, quant, prompt version) tuples and reducing the number of simultaneous shadow targets.
